On the night of 18 April 2030, in the private room of a ryōtei near Tsukiji, Kisaragi Genzō (77), chairman of the board of Kisaragi Shōji, lost feeling in his tongue and could no longer speak at the end of a fugu dinner; he collapsed at 22.40 and died on the way to hospital.

At the table: his daughter Kisaragi Sayuri, his son-in-law and finance director Hayashi Tōru, his secretary Ikeda Mai. The meal was prepared by the ryōtei’s fugu chef Ōmura Takeshi; the table was run by the okami, Fujimoto Kazue.

First assessment: fugu poisoning; the chef’s licence was suspended.

What did your husband think of the Paris sale?

The waste box and the jug cleared the fish; the poison was only in the cup. The corridor camera gave the pause, the okami the serving, the driver the package, the lab inventory the signature, the car the ampoule, and the phone the ‘Done’ message and E.V.
At the table every eye was on the chef’s knife. The poison came from the last and most respectful-looking hand.
Tsukiji — April 2030

Kisaragi Genzō understood that the company believed to be the final buyer of the Arendt notebook was only an intermediary, and that the goods, bowls and transfers were flowing to Paris. On 18 April he cancelled the Paris sale and said at the table that on Monday he would tell bube everything. His son-in-law Hayashi Tōru, warned by an e-mail signed ‘E.V.’, broke the tetrodotoxin ampoule he had had collected from the company’s laboratory the day before into the hirezake cup, lit the flame himself and handed the cup to his father-in-law with his own hand.
